name: tokio
why: The canonical Rust async runtime; heavy macro and feature-gated duplication.

ceilings.rationale: 7168 MB is the memory of a standard GitHub Actions runner. The documented Nimblesite/Deslop action must be able to analyse a repository this size without being OOM-killed, so the runner limit is the ceiling rather than an invented number. The wall ceiling is deliberately loose - it exists to catch a hang, not to police throughput.

must_find_status: NOT YET CURATED. No recall assertion runs for this repository until duplicates here are hand-verified by diffing the reported ranges. An empty list asserts nothing - it must never be read as evidence that recall is good.

must_find_type2.why: The two standard-stream handles are one module written twice. Both declare the same struct wrapping SplitByUtf8BoundaryIfWindows<Blocking<std::io::X>>, the same constructor, the same AsRawFd/AsFd/AsRawHandle/AsHandle impls behind the same cfg gates, and the same AsyncWrite impl.
must_find_type2.verified: diff of tokio/src/io/stderr.rs against tokio/src/io/stdout.rs changes only the renamed symbols - Stderr/Stdout, stderr()/stdout(), io::stderr()/io::stdout(), std::io::Stderr/std::io::Stdout - on every declaration and impl header. The only non-rename difference is extra doc-comment examples in stdout.rs; no statement differs.

must_find_type2_status: CURATED. Hand-verified by diffing the two files: the differences are renamed identifiers plus doc prose, so this is Type-2 and not byte-identical - it cannot reach the `identical` bucket. This is the Rust half of the curated Type-2 ground truth; nest carries the TypeScript half, so a language-specific recall regression cannot hide behind the other.
